case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed where DCYF developed four case plans tailored to the mother's issues and the Family Court correctly concluded the department satisfied its statutory reasonable-efforts obligation notwithstanding her non-compliance.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading recent Rhode Island authority on the reasonable-efforts finding in court-ordered case planning.
key_cases.quote: we are of the opinion that the Family Court justice correctly concluded that DCYF complied with its statutory obligation to make reasonable efforts to reunify respondent with Violet

key_cases.holding: The Court vacated the portion of the termination decree resting on the mother's mental deficiency under § 15-7-7(a)(2)(i) for lack of legally competent evidence, affirmed unfitness on another ground, and quashed as moot DCYF's certiorari petition about ending visitation pending appeal.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion describes the enhanced supervised visitation and parenting services DCYF must actually deliver before relying on a parent's failure to benefit.
key_cases.quote: Reversing the Family Court's decision to terminate Mary Ann's parental rights pursuant to § 15-7-7(a)(2)(i) (mental deficiency), we vacate that portion of the TPR decree.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed because DCYF's case plans were targeted to the conduct that caused removal and the father refused to complete them, and the Court reiterated that DCYF need not show extraordinary efforts to reunite parent and child.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies the ceiling that In re Violet G. does not state expressly, because the Court confirms that extraordinary efforts are not required and that reasonable efforts are assessed case by case against the parent's own cooperation.
key_cases.quote: the services offered were patently targeted to address the reasons that Lauren and Stephanie were placed into care

key_cases.holding: Both termination decrees were vacated: DCYF failed to make reasonable efforts as to the mother because it never offered substance-abuse treatment for what it identified as her primary barrier to reunification, and the father's unfitness was never proved by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Rhode Island decision most useful to a parent arguing that court-ordered services were misdirected, because the remedy was vacatur of the termination rather than deference to the department's choices.
key_cases.quote: due process requires that, before the state may terminate a parent's rights in his or her children, the state must support its allegations by clear and convincing evidence

key_cases.holding: Termination of the non-Indian mother's rights to an Indian child was affirmed: ICWA applied, DCYF's efforts were active efforts, and the required qualified expert witness may be qualified in any relevant field where the case raises no culturally-relevant issues.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion is the Rhode Island Supreme Court's fullest description of what ICWA 'active efforts' demand of DCYF, a standard higher than the ordinary reasonable-efforts obligation in a court-ordered service plan.
key_cases.quote: while at least one qualified expert witness is necessary under § 1912(f), that expert may be qualified in any relevant area if, as here, the case presents no culturally-relevant issues
